MeridianIQ API reference

contract v0.44.0 base URL /api

The full platform contract, grouped by area. Generated from lib/api-spec/openapi.yaml — the same file the server's request validation and the apps' typed clients are generated from, so this page can never disagree with the running API of the same version (GET /api/healthz reports the server's contract version).

Authentication

Two credentials, resolved in this order:

  • Firm API keys (machine callers) — Authorization: Bearer mk_…. A firm admin mints keys under Console → API & webhooks; the secret is shown once and only its hash is stored. A key is pinned to its firm and carries exactly the capability list it was minted with, from a deliberately narrow allowlist: invoice.read (pull invoice data), invoice.write (create/edit drafts), statement.write (push bank statements). No key can submit to the government rails, touch Clerk, billing or identity, or mint further credentials. Revocation is immediate — a revoked or unknown key is a clean 401, never a fall-through to another credential.
  • Sessions (the web apps & mobile) — an HttpOnly cookie (or the same signed token as Authorization: Bearer on mobile). Cookie-authenticated state-changing requests must also send the CSRF header x-meridian-csrf: 1; Bearer requests are exempt (they carry no cookie).

Webhooks & signatures

A firm admin registers HTTPS endpoints (POST /api/firm-webhooks) against a closed event catalogue: invoice.stamped, invoice.settled, statement.reconciled. Each delivery is a JSON POST carrying the event in x-meridian-event and a signature in x-meridian-signature.

Signature scheme — the signing secret (whsec_…) is shown once at registration; the HMAC key is its SHA-256 hash as lowercase hex, not the secret itself. Verify: HMAC-SHA256(rawBody, sha256hex(secret)), hex-encoded, must equal the header. Always verify over the raw body bytes:

import { createHash, createHmac } from "node:crypto";

// Hash your stored whsec_ secret ONCE — that hash is the HMAC key.
const key = createHash("sha256").update(process.env.WEBHOOK_SECRET).digest("hex");

function verify(rawBody, signatureHeader) {
  const expected = createHmac("sha256", key).update(rawBody).digest("hex");
  return expected === signatureHeader; // x-meridian-signature
}

Failed deliveries retry with exponential backoff up to 5 attempts, then park as dead; the per-endpoint delivery log (GET /api/firm-webhooks/{id}/deliveries) shows every attempt, and a dead delivery can be re-queued for a fresh attempt cycle (POST …/deliveries/{deliveryId}/retry). Disabling an endpoint stops deliveries and keeps its history.

Pointer-only payloads

Everything that leaves the platform — webhook bodies, alert messages — is pointer-only by construction: an entity type, an id and a timestamp, never amounts, party names, TINs or document content. A mis-registered or compromised receiver URL learns only that something happened; resolve the details back through this authenticated API (typically with an API key holding invoice.read).

Rate limits & errors

  • 600 requests/minute per principal in general; 60/minute on AI-powered (model-calling) routes. Each API key gets its own budget. A 429 answers with how long to wait.
  • Errors are {"error": "human-readable message"} with a conventional status: 400 invalid input, 401 unauthenticated, 403 not allowed, 404 outside your scope, 409 state moved (e.g. a duplicate payment intent or a stale lifecycle transition).
  • Mutating calls are transactional: a 4xx/5xx response means the request's writes were rolled back.
